title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page closes a notational section and begins the conceptual setup for 'invariants' of simplicial sets.

(1) Notation. Iterated constructions such as A^{*}_{*}^{**} = (((A^*)_*)^*)^* are allowed. Following the previous page, an upper star means cosimplicial (functors from Δ) and a lower star means simplicial (functors from Δ°). Objects of these categories are written with correspondingly starred letters, e.g. K^{**}_{**}^{*}.

(2) Proposition 1, stating that Δ^* (the Yoneda embedding Δ → Δ̂ = Ss) is the universal cosimplicial object.
(a) Let A be a category with colimits. Evaluation at Δ^*, F ↦ F(Δ^*), gives an equivalence between colimit-preserving functors Ss → A and cosimplicial objects of A, A^* = Hom(Δ, A).
(b) Let B be a category with limits. Evaluation at the simplicial object (Δ^*)° of Ss°, F ↦ F((Δ^*)°), gives an equivalence between functors Ss° → B sending colimits of Ss to limits of B and simplicial objects of B, B_* = Hom(Δ°, B).

Grothendieck remarks that:
- (b) is (a) applied to A = B°.
- (a) says that restriction along Yoneda, Hom(Ĉ, A) → Hom(C, A), is an equivalence on the cocontinuous part. This holds for any small C and is well known: Ĉ is the free cocompletion.
- The inverse is the left Kan extension, the 'realization' X ↦ colim over the simplex category Δ/X of φ(Δ^n).
- Dually, the inverse in (b) is X ↦ lim over (Δ/X)° of ψ([n]).

(3) Yoga.
- Covariant invariants of simplicial sets X with values in A that commute with colimits are the same as cosimplicial objects of A.
- Contravariant invariants with values in B that turn colimits into limits are the same as simplicial objects of B.
- For B = Sets these are simplicial sets K, and the invariant is the representable X ↦ Hom(X, K). This is continued on the next page.

The purpose is to set up a programme. The 'gross' invariants given by (co)simplicial objects are not homotopy invariant. One then adds structure (chain complexes, cosimplicial algebras; Dold–Kan on the next page) and localizes at maps coming from weak equivalences. This prepares the divided-power de Rham complex / cosimplicial-algebra models of homotopy types.
errors: Index-variance slip. In the inverse of (a), the cosimplicial object φ: Δ → A is written K_* with values K_{[n]}. By the convention of the previous page (lower star = Δ°-indexed) it should be K^* and K^{[n]}.

The same slip occurs in (b). The simplicial object ψ: Δ° → B is written K^* with values K^{[n]}; it should be K_* and K_{[n]}. The upper and lower stars are swapped consistently in both inverse formulas.

Minor imprecision. In (b), 'commutant aux lim' should be read as: the contravariant functor sends colimits in Ss to limits in B. Equivalently, it commutes with limits as a functor on Ss°. The statement is correct in substance.

ideas.what: Colimit-preserving functors from simplicial sets (presheaves on C) to a cocomplete A are equivalent to functors C → A (cosimplicial objects), via left Kan extension / realization along the category of simplices
ideas.modern_name: Universal property of presheaf category as free cocompletion; nerve–realization adjunction
ideas.usually_credited_to: Kan (1958, adjoint functors); folklore / SGA4 Exp. I
ideas.where_published: SGA 4, Exposé I (extension of functors to presheaf categories)

ideas.what: Dual statement: limit-sending contravariant functors on Ss correspond to simplicial objects of B; for B = Sets these are representable by simplicial sets
ideas.modern_name: Dual Kan extension; representability of continuous presheaf-valued functors

ideas.what: Yoga: 'gross' (co)continuous invariants of homotopy types are given by (co)simplicial objects; refined homotopy invariants are obtained by adding structure and localizing at maps induced by weak equivalences
ideas.modern_name: Homotopical algebra / derived functors via localization (model-category philosophy)
ideas.where_published: Similar philosophy in Pursuing Stacks (1983) and Les Dérivateurs

deep.surprise_reason: The page states a standard, well-known universal property (Grothendieck himself calls it 'bien connu') and a programmatic yoga. There is no new result here.
transcription_corrections: '$= \mathcal{B}\mathcal{S}^*$ [?]' at the top is likely a stray marginal annotation (something like '= Ob S^*'), not mathematical content.
The line read as 'Le rôle de $\Delta^* \in \hat{\Delta}^*$' contains a crossed-out symbol; it reads roughly 'Δ^* ∈ Ob Δ̂^*'.

Near 'Hom comm. à lim' in the lower-left, the transcription reads 'C'est vrai pour une [-toute (petite)-] catégorie C'. The image suggests the uncrossed reading 'toute (petite) catégorie C', with the inserted word 'une' above it; the sense is 'for any small category C'.
In the yoga, '[-commutent aux X_*-]' is a crossed-out phrase; the intended text is 'qui commutent aux lim p.r. à X_*'.
